authoredAnchors.text: You begin with the table because beginning with a person is impossible. Object one: ceramic cup, blue glaze, repaired handle. Object two: six pencils, five ordinary, one carpenter's pencil shortened to the width of two fingers. Object three: folding knife with no blade, used as a paperweight. Each description is true. None explains why Ivo kept it.

At the bottom of the kitchen drawer, underneath rubber bands and a warranty for a kettle that is no longer here, you find your own name. It is written on a cream envelope. ADA, IF YOU COME. The second half of the sentence hurts more than the first.

Ada. This is not an apology in advance. I dislike that trick. A letter cannot make a demand of someone simply by outliving its writer. The cloth belongs to the lens cover. The catalogue belongs to you. If the work stops being work and becomes something else, you may leave. Ask Tomas about the tapes. Ask Nessa what the map leaves out. Do not assume I have given either of them the whole of anything. I.

You read it again, this time resisting the urge to treat its omissions as a puzzle he meant you to solve. A person can be secretive without being wise. A dead person can still waste your time. You put the letter in an acid-free sleeve anyway, because being angry is not a preservation method.

activity.prompt: What should Ada record about the unopened replacement remote?
options: Its presence and condition, with the reason for keeping it unknown.
Proof that Ivo planned every object as a clue.
A definite story about why he disliked it.
activity.explanation: Observation can be catalogued while motive remains unknown.

authoredAnchors.text: The television remote has been repaired with tape. The tape has then been labeled so its raised edge does not obscure the volume button. An unopened replacement remote sits in a drawer beneath it. You can imagine Ivo ordering the new one, discovering it did not feel right, and making a principle out of keeping the old. You can also imagine being wrong. Your work is full of plausible little stories with no witness left to contradict them.
Two remote controls. One in active use, inferred from wear and placement. One boxed. Reason for retaining both unknown.

Unknown begins to feel less like a failure of the catalogue than a way of keeping it honest. You could write uncertainty on almost everything in the room. Instead, you distinguish it: what you do not know yet, what somebody else may know, and what no available source is likely to answer.

activity.prompt: What is the strongest claim the first documentation supports?
options: The machine guarantees everyone is safe.
Ivo sent a message from the afterlife.
Two people documented a dated trace whose origin is unknown.
activity.explanation: Witnesses and photographs establish the observation, not its mechanism or authority.

activity.prompt: What is the best immediate response to the bell trace?
options: Operate the unknown controls to test its promise.
Ask a qualified person to inspect and keep the shaft clear.
Assume a hidden author has guaranteed safety.
activity.explanation: The witnessed wording justifies investigation; it does not replace an inspection.

chapter1Audit.plan: Wrong answers receive explanatory feedback without shame, penalty or canonical/save mutation. No new story, gates, chronology or models; two adjacent inventory activities only.

ch1_s2_evidence: Ada: The repaired handle is visible. The cup does not tell us whether Ivo expected me; that would turn an observation into a claim about his intention.
Ada: Blue glaze, repaired handle: those are things I can record from the cup itself. Why he kept it remains a separate question.
Ada: I can describe the cup, pencils and paperweight. Their presence does not establish that Ivo left each one as a clue.
ch1_s2a_evidence: Ada: One remote is worn and taped; the replacement is still boxed. I can record their condition and placement while leaving the reason for keeping both unknown.
Ada: A boxed replacement tells us what is here, not that every object was arranged as a clue. The catalogue can keep the reason unknown.
Ada: I can imagine that the replacement did not feel right to him. There is no witness for that story, so I cannot record his dislike as a fact.
